concepts.name: Tail release
concepts.direction: Let the lower-right Q tail continue into ONE short, slightly curving warm-beige watercolor brush gesture. The portion nearest the geometric Q is crisp and pigment-rich; the outer end softens and thins into a faint diffuse wash. Keep the Q's actual tail legible and the total gesture contained within the central safe area. The gesture should feel like a restrained release of ink from a precise mark, never smoke, a feather, a flourish of handwriting, or a large splash.
concepts.prompt:
Use case: logo-brand / precise-object-edit.
Edit target: the attached existing AI Tech Review icon. Produce ONE finished square app-icon artwork, 1024 by 1024, full bleed, not a mockup or comparison sheet.
Preserve the recognizable geometric Q, its position and size, and the exactly TWO round muted teal nodes joined by ONE short diagonal segment inside the Q. Preserve the generous safe area. Preserve the dark matte burgundy background near #3F1D2B, the subdued warm beige Q near #B39B79, and patina teal near #6F9185. The user explicitly rejected bright versions; keep the result dark, restrained, and quiet.
Add only ONE or TWO intentional artistic watercolor gestures as described below. They must have convincing pigment granulation, subtle pooling, paperlike dry-edge irregularity, and a controlled transition from a crisp painted edge into a faint translucent wash. This is an elegant scientific editorial identity, not a decorative watercolor illustration. Keep the Q and the two-node relationship dominant and readable as a home-screen icon and at 32 pixels. The background may retain only an extremely quiet trace of the original grain. Flat matte surface with no shine or 3D effects.
No text other than the existing Q shape, no new letters, no frame, no white/pale background, no flowers, no atom ellipses, no feathers, no stars, no sparkles, no glowing neon, no drop shadow, no extra nodes, no decorative splatter field, no watermark.

concepts.name: Pigment orbit
concepts.direction: Place ONE asymmetrical crescent-shaped watercolor gesture close to the outer upper-left shoulder of the Q, lightly echoing a short portion of the ring without becoming a second complete ring or an atomic orbit. Use muted beige/umber pigment, a crisp anchoring start, and a softly dispersing tapered end. Integrate it tightly with the mark's balance and leave the core Q fully geometric and the interior nodes unobscured. The gesture should be small, tactile, and visibly hand-painted, not a background halo.

concepts.name: Two-stroke counterpoint
concepts.direction: Add exactly TWO short, restrained watercolor brush gestures in visual counterpoint: a low warm-beige sweep near the Q's lower-left quadrant and a shorter muted-patina-teal touch near its upper-right shoulder. Their orientations should gently converse rather than cross over or obscure the Q or nodes. Each gesture should go from one deliberate crisp edge to a thin, softly diffused wash. The two strokes should introduce painterly rhythm with ample negative space, never a wreath, a pair of wings, or background blobs.

concepts.name: Wet-edge Q
concepts.direction: Integrate watercolor into the Q itself rather than placing an extra ornament. Across only a short upper-left arc of the Q, transition the precise warm-beige outer edge into a delicately granulated wet-on-damp edge that feathers outward and fades into the burgundy. Preserve the inner edge and the full Q topology, keep most of the Q crisp, preserve the tail and the two interior nodes exactly. This should read as ONE deliberate painted arc with a crisp-to-diffuse transition, not corrosion, a damaged ring, fuzzy antialiasing, or an eroded letter.
